items.label: text
items.text: Alkenes are unsaturated compounds because they contain a C=C bond. A saturated compound contains single C-C bonds only whereas an unsaturated compound contains one or more double or triple C-C bonds.

items.label: text
items.text: Alkenes have the general formula CH2. The number of hydrogen atoms is twice the number of carbon atoms. This means that all alkenes have the same empirical formula, CH2.

items.label: text
items.text: The alkene with 11 carbon atoms will have 22 hydrogen atoms and the molecular formula C11H_22.

items.label: text
items.text: These are very similar to those of the alkanes. Remember that the small alkanes with up to four carbon atoms are gases at room temperature. The same is true for the alkenes. They are gases up to C4H8, and the next dozen or so are liquids. Again, the members of the homologous series show a trend in physical properties.

items.label: text
items.text: This isn't a reaction anybody would ever choose to do. Alkenes are much too useful to waste by burning them.

items.label: text
items.text: The C=C double bond is the functional group. The functional group determines the chemical properties of a compound. Alkenes have characteristic chemical properties which are different from those of alkanes. Alkenes are much more reactive than alkanes.

items.label: text
items.text: Alkenes undergo addition reactions. Part of the double bond breaks to become a single C-C bond and the electrons are used to join other atoms onto the two carbon atoms.
